preRevision.revision_idea: Add quadratic air drag to the Duffing law so losses grow with speed as well as with slow viscous drag. The leftover misses still swing with each bob and are biggest during fast motion, which points to missing speed-dependent damping.

truth.note: This clip was rendered from a law drawn by public randomness (drand round 6605124). The round was named in 493e869 and pushed before it existed; the law's SHA-256 was pushed in 8337791 before the clip was rendered; the run used commit edb5c02 on a clean tree; the law was revealed in 3636e41. Found. The drawn law was a cubic hardening spring with quadratic damping. The referee asked for quadratic air drag on Muse Spark's Duffing law, and Muse Wonder's one try kept a viscous term that fitted to 0.000 ± 0.005 (absent under the rule) beside the cubic stiffness and quadratic drag. Every constant lands within 1.4σ, and it misses the unseen frames by 1.3 times the noise. With no ruler found, lengths are in pixels; true values in pixels use the render's own scale.

sealed.rule: found only if the winner's term set equals the drawn term set, a fitted term whose constant is within 2σ of zero counting as absent, and every shared constant is within 2σ of the drawn value
sealed.terms: winner: linear (ω), viscous γ = 0.000 ± 0.005 (0σ, absent), cubic α (280σ, present), quadratic drag β (96σ, present); drawn: linear, cubic, quadratic drag. Term sets equal.
